preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard echo  |  Medium = targeted test or genetic panel ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = advanced imaging CT/MRI ($1,500–$5,000+)

questions.question: Does 2D echo show bicuspid aortic valve morphology (2 cusps, raphe visible on parasternal short axis)?
Is there doming or restricted cusp opening on echo?
Is there aortic root or ascending aorta dilation (Z-score >2 in children; >4.0 cm in adults)?
Does CT/MRI angiography confirm bicuspid morphology and aortic dimensions?
Is there a systolic ejection murmur at the right upper sternal border?
Is there an ejection click (early systolic click at apex or base)?
Is there a diastolic murmur suggesting aortic regurgitation?
Is there a first-degree relative with confirmed BAV?
Is there a family history of aortic aneurysm or dissection?
Is there a known associated genetic condition (Turner syndrome, Williams syndrome, coarctation family history)?
Is there an elevated peak aortic valve gradient on Doppler (>20 mmHg mild; >40 mmHg moderate)?
Is there an aortic regurgitation jet on color Doppler?
Is there LV hypertrophy on echo (from chronic pressure overload)?
Is there a confirmed coarctation of the aorta? (BAV coexists in 50–70% of coarctation cases)
Is there a history of endocarditis? (BAV is #1 risk factor for native valve endocarditis)
Is there exertional dyspnea, chest pain, or syncope?
Is there reduced exercise tolerance documented on stress test?

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: BAV confirmed or highly probable; proceed to surveillance protocol with serial echo; referral to cardiology for aortic root monitoring; genetic counseling for first-degree relatives

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: diagnostic echo indicated if not yet completed; screening of first-degree relatives warranted given autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: insufficient evidence; screening echo warranted if family history or associated findings present; reassess if new clinical findings emerge
